summary: Create masked cross-cloud service-account chaining pattern for QA environment to limit elevation surface
description:
Issue summary:
We need a short-lived, masked service-account chaining pattern for the QA environment that allows CI jobs to access both a GCP storage bucket and an AWS S3 read-only path without exposing broad cross-account permissions. Current ad-hoc chains are granting broad assume-role permissions and we observed two near-miss cases where elevated permissions were reused across jobs.

Impact:
- Increased blast radius for QA CI jobs that run model validation and data staging (potential to affect internal datasets).
- Manual workflows to provision least-privileged role chaining are slow and error-prone.
- Security team flagged non-auditable implicit role assumption in recent audit.

Environment:
- QA project namespace: redwood-qa-ops (GCP)
- AWS account: rwd-qa-data (us-east-1)
- CI runner: ephemeral-gke-qa cluster
- Time window observed: 2026-03-05 to 2026-03-09

Steps to reproduce (example job):
1) CI creates a short-lived GCP service account key via gcloud iam service-accounts keys create (simulated by runner).
2) Job exchanges credentials against GCP Workload Identity Federation and invokes a custom token broker to assume AWS role rwd-qa-batch-role.
3) Token broker issues an AWS STS AssumeRole with inline session policy to limit S3 path.
4) Some jobs re-use the broker session and unexpectedly gain access to broader S3 prefixes due to missing session-policy enforcement.

Observed logs / errors:
- aws sts AssumeRole: success (but returned credentials had no session policy applied for two jobs)
- gcloud auth: WARN: service account key created for long duration (audit flagged)
- Broker logs: "session_policy_not_applied: policy-eval-mismatch" (2026-03-07T14:22:03Z)

Request:
- Design and provision a reusable pattern (service-account + broker) that produces masked, audited, and automatically-expiring cross-cloud credentials narrowly scoped per-job, and implement in QA.
- Provide a short runbook for CI teams and add monitoring/alerting for session-policy mismatch events.
comments: 2026-03-10: Maya Chen - Initial report and request for scoped chaining pattern. Asked for SRE and Sec review.

2026-03-11: Diego Alvarez - I can prototype a broker that mints AWS STS creds with session policies bound and uses GCP Workload Identity as the gate. Need confirmation on allowed S3 prefixes and audit retention requirements.

2026-03-11: Priya Nair (Security) - We require permission boundaries and explicit deny on any write operations. Audit logs must be retained 90 days and correlated with CI job IDs. Also request MFA or JIT approval for any privileged escalation beyond read-only.

2026-03-12: Diego Alvarez - Prototype deployed to staging: service account 'qa-role-broker@redwood-qa-ops.iam.gserviceaccount.com' plus AWS role 'qa-broker-arn' with trust policy restricted to broker. Observed failing test where session tag exceeded length; adding tag normalization fallback.

2026-03-13: SRE (Anya Volkov) - Confirmed prototype enforces session policy and permission boundary. Ran 10 synthetic jobs, no leakage observed. Will schedule rollout to QA next week behind feature flag.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered:
- Broker not attaching inline session policy (bug in token-flow) -> reproduced in unit tests.
- STS AssumeRole returned credentials but AWS ignored session policy due to missing 'sts:TagSession' call before policy evaluation -> found a mismatch in how tags were passed from GCP token exchange.
Findings:
- Broker code path omitted 'TagSession' for jobs that used the legacy exchange endpoint.
- Session tags occasionally exceeded 256 characters when CI job metadata was concatenated; AWS rejected the tags silently and fell back to default role permissions.
- No single incident of data exfiltration found, but audit showed two instances where broader list-bucket access would have been possible.
Actions taken during triage:
- Disabled legacy exchange endpoint for QA and enforced max tag length and normalization in broker.
- Patched broker to always call TagSession and attach an inline session policy constructed from CI job ID and repo path.
- Added a CloudWatch metric and GCP log entry when TagSession returns a tag-length error.
resolution:
Workaround/fix implemented:
- Deployed 'qa-role-broker' with the following controls: enforced TagSession usage, inline session policies limiting S3 prefixes, permission boundary 'rwd-qa-broker-boundary' that denies write operations, and automatic 15-minute credential TTL.
- Updated GCP service account IAM binding to allow only the broker to impersonate, and rotated any long-lived keys found during audit.
- Added an alert rule: 'broker.session_policy_mismatch' to #oncall and set PagerDuty for P1 occurrences.
Rollout notes:
- Feature flagged rollout scheduled for 2026-03-17 to QA; manual enable per CI queue.
- Runbook added to Confluence with example CI snippets and enforcement policy.
Follow-ups:
- INT-227800: create automated CI linting rule to prevent long job-metadata fields (new ticket planned).
- Security to run a 30-day audit of all QA broker transactions and report back.
- Consider upstreaming broker pattern to Dedicated onboarding flow.
